Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroTech Dynamics Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroTech Dynamics' Q3 Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Lopez, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Whitaker, Chief Strategy Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. AeroTech Dynamics delivered a solid performance in the third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across defense, commercial aerospace, and space systems. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Today, we'll cover key areas including the performance of our priority defense programs, overall company performance highlights and key takeaways, our strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and full year, updates on key programs like development milestones and production ramps, revenue and earnings guidance by segment, backlog growth both in absolute terms and percentage change, program margins and cost performance analysis, and an analysis of our revenue drivers and headwinds. We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our Next-Generation Air Dominance or NGAD program and its potential to drive transformative growth in air dominance capabilities for decades to come. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily as global travel rebounds.

With that, I'll turn it over to John Harlan, our CFO, for a deep dive into the financials and these key aspects.

John Harlan:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Let's turn to the financials and a detailed review of our performance. In Q3, we reported revenue of $2.6 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year and 8% sequentially on an organic basis, exceeding our guidance midpoint. Our adjusted earnings per share came in at $2.85, beating expectations by 12%. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $1.5 billion in cash and equivalents, low net leverage at 1.8 times, and robust free cash flow of $350 million after capex investments. Our guidance for the full year remains on track, and we're actively managing costs while investing in high-return growth areas like hypersonics and autonomy. We're also committed to returning capital through $1.2 billion in share repurchases and an 8% dividend increase to $0.45 per share.

Gross margins expanded to 16.5%, operating income reached $420 million, reflecting favorable program mix and productivity gains. Now, let me provide more color on our performance across priority defense programs, which continue to drive the majority of our Aeronautics, Missiles & Space, and related segments. These programs generated $4.2 billion in Q3 revenue, up 18% year-over-year, accounting for 62% of total defense bookings. Our funded backlog is $28.7 billion, with total backlog over $112 billion—a 12% sequential increase—supported by multi-year awards from the U.S. Department of Defense, Foreign Military Sales partners, and Indo-Pacific allies.

Starting with our Next-Generation Air Dominance family, including the stealth fighter and collaborative combat aircraft enablers—this is our flagship effort. Lot 12 low-rate initial production deliveries are ahead of schedule; we handed over 14 aircraft this quarter, pushing year-to-date to 38, up from 29 last year, with 98.5% mission-capable rates in tests at Edwards Air Force Base. Revenue reached $1.8 billion, up 22%, and EBITA margins grew 150 basis points to 12.4% from favorable estimate-at-completion adjustments and fixed-price efficiencies via our digital twin engineering. We've incorporated Block 4 upgrades with AI sensor fusion and open mission systems, cutting integration times 35% per Joint Program Office reviews. Demand is strong—a $2.1 billion indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity task order for CCA prototypes from the Air Force, plus commitments from the UK and Japan under AUKUS Pillar II. We're addressing supply risks like titanium and rare earths through dual-sourcing with Australian partners, setting up for full-rate production in fiscal 2025 and export potential.

Next, Integrated Air and Missile Defense, led by Aegis upgrades and hypersonic interceptors, posted $1.1 billion in revenue, up 25%, with $3.4 billion in new bookings including a $1.2 billion sole-source for Glide Phase Interceptor development. We delivered 22 Aegis Baseline 10 systems to DDG-51 Flight III destroyers, with shakedowns on time at Bath Iron Works. Margins held at 13.2% despite 7% composite inflation, thanks to Value Engineering Change Proposals using additive manufacturing that reduced costs 18%. Our 300kW laser demonstrator hit 45 seconds of dwell against hypersonic targets in Pacific tests, on path for HELIOS Increment 2 by 2026. Middle East demand is surging—$900 million FMS from Saudi Arabia for Patriot GEM-T, UAE THAAD expansions—while Europe's NATO Eastern Flank added $450 million from Poland's Wisla analog. We're positioned for $5-7 billion in Army funding from supplementals, leading in JADC2 with open architecture.

Our Unmanned and Autonomy portfolio exploded to $850 million revenue, up 32%, with backlog doubling to $9.2 billion on a $2.8 billion Replicator award for attritable UAS. We flight-tested 150 Collaborative Autonomous Teaming drones, hitting 95% swarm autonomy in contested electromagnetic interference during Project Convergence Capstone 4. Margins rose to 11.8% with scaled GaN AESA production in Huntsville. This aligns with DoD's affordable mass shift against Chinese swarms—our platforms offer 5x loiter time at one-third TB-2 cost. Australia ordered $600 million Ghost Bat for NGAD integration, Taiwan in talks amid Strait tensions. We're spending $250 million on AI/ML stacks, partnering with Palantir for JADC2 data lakes.

Finally, Space Domain Awareness and Resilient Missile Warning contributed $450 million, up 15%, with a $1.5 billion Tranche 2 Transport Layer contract under SDA's Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture. Three HBTSS pathfinders launched via SpaceX, achieving full checkout and hypersonic tracking for NORTHCOM. Margins at 14.1% from vertical photonics integration. Europe's IRIS² yields $300 million NATO deals, Japan seeks cueing against DPRK threats. Our cyber-resilient mesh networking showed zero exploits in red-team tests.

Overall, defense revenue grew 19% to $6.8 billion, ROIC 22.4%. Labor delays at Fort Worth and titanium tariffs added pressures, but 40% domestic content and $1.2 billion forward pricing derisk us. With FY24 NDAA at $886 billion and supplementals, our $250 billion funnel targets 12-15% organic growth in FY25 at 3.5x book-to-bill.

Shifting to overall company performance highlights and key takeaways, Q3 underscores our resilience. Revenue of $2.52 billion beat guidance by $50 million—eighth straight double-digit growth quarter. Full-year now $10.4-10.8 billion, 11-15% up. Defense Systems at 55% grew 15% to $1.39 billion on F-35 sustainment and NGAD LRIP, plus $450 million hypersonic award. Missiles & Space up 18% to $630 million with GBSD motors, JASSM-ER exports, ULA Vulcan stake. Commercial Aerospace up 5% to $378 million on 777X aerostructures, E2 winglets despite titanium shortages. Emerging C4ISR up 25% to $126 million on DEW for MQ-9.

Adjusted EBITDA $415 million or 16.5%, up 180 bps from fixed-price mix and $25 million Lean Sigma savings. Segment margins: Defense 18.2%, Missiles 17.8%, Commercial 12.1%. GAAP EPS $1.72, beat by $0.14. Cash flow $450 million operating, $320 million free. Funded backlog $18.5 billion up 14%, total $28.2 billion at 1.25x book-to-bill. Geopolitics: DoD $850 billion, $60 billion Ukraine aid, AUKUS $2 billion pipeline.

Key takeaways: Defense upcycle with $2.2 trillion global spend; commercial inflection at 4.7 billion passengers; international to 22% from Asia/Europe/Middle East. Risks like 4% supply inflation mitigated by 65% fixed-price, recent UAV acquisition.

On strategic priorities and outlook, our three pillars—technological superiority, execution, global expansion—guide us. Accelerating hypersonics: Dark Eagle 95% test success, LRIP Q1 2025, $450 million R&D for 2027 full-rate, ATLAS AI for kill chains. Autonomy: MQ-Next with $1.2 billion CCA orders, 300kW laser at 50% efficiency. Execution: F-35 Block 4 $3.2 billion, 13.5% margins, supply resilience at 92% score. International: Patriot to Poland/Romania $1.8 billion, Saudi P-8A $900 million, AUKUS/GCAP.

Q4 revenue $2.55-2.65 billion: Aeronautics $1.25 billion (10% up, 12-12.5% margins), Missiles $820 million (12%, 14.5-15%), Space $510 million (7%, 11-11.5%). FY24 $9.85-9.95 billion, EPS $11.20-11.40. FY25 $10.9-11.3 billion, EPS $12.50-13.00, margins 13-13.5%. Risks: CRs, inflation hedged 70%.

For updates on key programs, our $148 billion backlog up 8% reflects demand. F-35: 156 Q3 deliveries (YTD 442, FY 620 target), Lot 20 Milestone C Q1 2025, Block 4 ECRs down 65%, FMS 28 jets. NGAD CDR complete, TRL 8, $2.8 billion risk reduction, CCA flights Q2 2025. Missiles: ARRW IOC mid-2025, 120/year, LRASM 95% success, 1,450 units up 22%, $22 billion backlog. SM-6 350 units. Rotary: FVL FLRAA 85% CDR, 450 test hours, $3.1 billion LRIP; CH-53K 20 early deliveries, 99.7% rates. Space: GPS IIIF two launches, $7.2 billion funded; Vulcan NSSL $1.1 billion. C4ISR: E-7 delivery, NGJ-MB exports $850 million. Q4 deliveries up 9%, $42.5 billion FY revenue.

Revenue and earnings guidance by segment: Commercial $28-30 billion FY24 (12-15% up, 13.5-14% margins) on 737/A320, SAF nacelles; 2025 $32-34 billion. Defense $42-44 billion (8-10%, 17.5-18%) on F-35 $12 billion, hypersonics $10 billion; 2025 $46-48 billion NGAD. Space $18-19 billion (10-12%, 16-17%) GPS/Orion; 2025 $20-21 billion. Total FY24 $88-93 billion, EPS $28.50-29.50, FCF $6-7 billion.

Backlog growth: Total $92.5 billion, up $12.8 billion or 16% YoY, $4.2 billion QoQ, 1.25x book-to-bill. Defense $58.2 billion up 21% ($10.1 billion) on F-35 $3.5 billion, hypersonics $2.8 billion, FMS $1.2 billion. Commercial $26.1 billion up 8%, wing orders $1.1 billion. Space $8.2 billion up 9%, Orion $900 million. FY24 over $100 billion.

Program margins and cost performance: Consolidated 10.8% up 110 bps, CPI 1.03. Aeronautics 11.5% F-35 CPI 1.08; Missiles 12.2% ARRW EAC favorable; Rotary 9.8% CH-53K 10.5%; Space 10.1% Orion CPI 1.05. $285 million favorable EACs, mix to sustainment, 85% EPA clauses.

Revenue drivers and headwinds: Drivers—commercial $9.8 billion up 22% OEM/MRO, defense $8.9 billion F-35/missiles, space $2.7 billion up 25%. Headwinds—GTF delays $350 million, titanium +40%, labor premiums; mitigated by inventory, digital twins. FY24 raised $84-86 billion.

That covers our financial story—strong execution positioning us for growth.

Maria Lopez:
Thank you, John. Operationally, we've improved supply chain management, ramping production on key programs like F-35 and NGAD. Investments in automation and digital tech, including robotic fiber placement at 70% capacity, are driving efficiency and cost reductions. We've built strategic inventory and dual-sourced critical materials, achieving 92% resilience scores while navigating inflation.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Maria. Technologically, we're advancing next-gen propulsion with adaptive cycle engines for NGAD, AI autonomy stacks, and 300kW lasers. These give us edge in hypersonics, swarms, and resilient C4ISR, with partnerships accelerating TRLs and integration.

Tom Whitaker:
Thank you, Elena. Strategically, we're evaluating tuck-in acquisitions in UAV autonomy and pursuing new models for uncrewed markets. For instance, our recent $300 million UAV buy scales us in $100 billion opportunity, complementing NGAD and AUKUS.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Tom. Marketing-wise, our branding campaign is succeeding, boosting awareness in defense and commercial. Digital channels are expanding reach, with results showing 20% uplift in international leads from Asia-Pacific and Europe.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Thompson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the backlog growth and how it breaks down across segments?

Alex Rivera:
Certainly, Mike. As John detailed, total backlog hit $92.5 billion, up 16% year-over-year with strong defense at 21% growth from F-35, hypersonics, and FMS. This 1.25x book-to-bill gives multi-year visibility, supporting our raised FY25 outlook.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Hi, thanks. I'm curious about program margins—any details on cost performance and EACs?

John Harlan:
Emily, margins expanded to 10.8% with $285 million favorable EACs, driven by F-35 learning curves at 92% efficiency, additive manufacturing savings, and sustainment mix. We're mitigating titanium volatility through offtake deals and localization.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Regarding the updates on key programs like NGAD and hypersonics?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
David, NGAD passed CDR with TRL 8, $2.8 billion risk reduction, CCA flights soon. Hypersonics like ARRW hit test milestones for IOC 2025, ramping production amid Indo-Pacific demand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim:
Question about revenue guidance by segment and any headwinds?

John Harlan:
Rachel, FY24 guidance firm: Defense $42-44 billion, Commercial $28-30 billion, Space $18-19 billion. Headwinds like GTF delays and titanium are transitory, offset by digital twins and hedging—expect low-teens growth into 2025.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation in a world needing advanced aerospace and defense solutions.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 earnings call. A replay will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
